partner_result.actual_application: A fair literal-coordinate bipartition gives W_h>=omega_h E_h/16; the partner inequality is then applied as ||p_Q||inf<=8e^(1/4)|a|^(-1/4)W_h^(-1/8).

new_results.statement: For A=D+R Lambda R^T with rank-three Parseval carrier, fixed physical h, K_h=r_hr_h^T+D_hh Lambda^{-1}, E_h=Delta^2 tr(K_h S_h K_h S_h), and omega_h the disjoint ordered pair-pair fraction, if A_hh, E_h, omega_h are nonzero then ||p_Q||inf <=8sqrt(2)e^(1/4)|A_hh|^-1/4 omega_h^-1/8 E_h^-1/8.
E_h>=3 Delta^(4/3)(1-c_h)^(4/3)|D_hh|^(4/3)|A_hh|^(2/3), using det K_h=D_hh^2 A_hh/det Lambda and det S_h=(1-c_h)^2.

When D_hh=0, the anchored pair law is exactly the Pluecker triple law conditioned on h. If all pair-coordinate marginals are <=3/8, Omega_h>=1/4 and a density bound follows; otherwise some j satisfies ||r_h wedge r_j||^2>3c_h/8. Under r46 three-hub hit one may choose c_h>7/24, so the collision alternative gives ||r_h wedge r_j||^2>7/64.

next_step: Starting from c_h>7/24, group the two literal hubs in the plane-localized branch and aggregate the remaining third carrier direction before any reciprocal physical determinant; separately route zero/near pivot, near-coloop, and small diagonal-twist endpoints without deleting nonzero tails.
